name: Paul-trap pseudopotential = ponderomotive potential
summary: The time-averaged force that holds an ion in an RF Paul trap is the same ponderomotive force that pushes electrons out of an intense laser focus (channel formation, wakefield bubbles). Ion micromotion is the electron's quiver motion.
breaks: For a_0\gtrsim1 the laser case becomes relativistic (cycle-averaged \gamma), which never happens in ion traps. A Paul trap also needs Mathieu stability (q\lesssim0.9), a condition with no counterpart in a laser focus.

name: High-frequency Floquet expansion gives ponderomotive force
summary: The Kapitza/Magnus high-frequency expansion used for Floquet engineering gives, at leading order, the ponderomotive Hamiltonian of laser–plasma theory. Both expansions fail near resonances, where driven heating starts.

name: Laser-cooled ion crystals are strongly coupled plasmas
summary: Laser-cooled ions in Paul and Penning traps reach Γ≫175 and form Coulomb crystals. These are one-component plasmas described by the same coupling parameter and Wigner–Seitz radius as dusty-plasma crystals. Their phonon modes are the quantum bus for trapped-ion gates, and 2D Penning-trap crystals are used as Ising simulators.
sources: Chu & I (1994). "Direct observation of Coulomb crystals and liquids in strongly coupled rf dusty plasmas". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 72, 4009. [doi:10.1103/PhysRevLett.72.4009](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevLett.72.4009)
Cirac & Zoller (1995). "Quantum Computations with Cold Trapped Ions". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 74, 4091. [doi:10.1103/PhysRevLett.74.4091](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevLett.74.4091)

name: Penning trap: cyclotron and E×B magnetron motion
summary: Penning traps hold charges using the drifts of plasma single-particle theory: the magnetron mode is the E×B drift in the trap's radial field. The same geometry (the Malmberg–Penning trap) holds non-neutral plasmas and the rotating 2D ion crystals used for quantum simulation.

name: Ultracold neutral plasmas from laser-cooled atoms
summary: Photoionizing laser-cooled atoms just above threshold makes neutral plasmas with electron temperatures of a few kelvin and sub-kelvin ions, reaching Γ>1. Disorder-induced heating caps ion coupling near Γ≈2–3; laser-cooling the plasma ions themselves pushes it higher.

name: Rydberg gases and ultracold plasmas interconvert
summary: Dense Rydberg gases avalanche-ionize on their own into ultracold plasmas. Ultracold plasmas in turn recombine, by three-body recombination, into high-n Rydberg states. So Rydberg-atom structure (how size and binding scale with n) controls both how the plasma forms and how it decays.

name: Adiabatic invariant μ ↔ conserved quantum number
summary: The magnetic moment μ that makes mirrors work is the gyration action, the classical counterpart of the quantum adiabatic theorem. Under slow change the Landau-level index is conserved, and μ=(n+1/2)|q|ħ/m. Ehrenfest's adiabatic hypothesis made this exact link in the old quantum theory.
breaks: In fusion plasmas n\sim10^7 for 10 keV electrons at 5 T, so only the classical invariant matters there. Classical μ is conserved only asymptotically (exponentially small breaking), while the quantum theorem needs a spectral gap.

name: Gyrophase anholonomy: geometric phase of gyration
summary: In guiding-centre theory, the gyrophase picks up a geometric shift when the field direction is carried around a loop (Littlejohn's gyrogauge connection). This is the classical Hannay angle; its quantum counterpart is the Berry phase of a Landau-level state.
map: \Delta\theta_g=\oint\mathbf R\cdot d\mathbf x,\ \mathbf R=(\nabla\hat e_1)\cdot\hat e_2\ \leftrightarrow\ \gamma_B=i\oint\langle n|\nabla n\rangle\cdot d\mathbf R
sources: Berry (1984). "Quantal phase factors accompanying adiabatic changes". *Proc. R. Soc. A* 392, 45. [doi:10.1098/rspa.1984.0023](https://doi.org/10.1098/rspa.1984.0023)

name: Chern numbers of magnetized plasma waves; edge modes
summary: Band-topology ideas built on Berry curvature have been applied to the cold magnetized-plasma dielectric. Its wave bands carry nonzero Chern numbers, and bulk–edge correspondence predicts one-way, backscatter-immune edge waves at plasma boundaries. Experimental confirmation is still pending.
sources: Berry (1984). "Quantal phase factors accompanying adiabatic changes". *Proc. R. Soc. A* 392, 45. [doi:10.1098/rspa.1984.0023](https://doi.org/10.1098/rspa.1984.0023)

name: Instability onset as PT breaking at a Krein collision
summary: Linearized ideal plasma and fluid systems have a PT-symmetric (G-Hamiltonian) structure. Two-stream and Kelvin–Helmholtz instabilities appear when a positive-action and a negative-action (negative-energy) mode collide at an exceptional point. This is the same PT-breaking transition studied in non-Hermitian photonics.
map: \omega\in\mathbb R\ \text{(PT unbroken)}\to(\omega,\omega^*)\ \text{at EP: Krein collision of }\pm\text{-action modes}
sources: Bender & Boettcher (1998). "Real Spectra in Non-Hermitian Hamiltonians Having PT Symmetry". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 80, 5243. [arXiv:physics/9712001](https://arxiv.org/abs/physics/9712001)

name: MHD energy principle = Rayleigh–Ritz variational principle
summary: Static ideal MHD has a self-adjoint force operator, so ω² is real, as for a Hermitian spectrum. Stability follows from minimizing δW over trial displacements, the same variational principle that bounds quantum ground-state energies. Equilibrium flows break self-adjointness (Frieman–Rotenberg).

name: Mode conversion ↔ Landau–Zener transitions
summary: Waves in inhomogeneous plasma are traced with WKB/eikonal rays, where cutoffs act as turning points. Where two dispersion branches nearly cross, linear mode conversion reduces to a 2×2 Landau–Zener problem along the ray. It gives the same exponential transmission law, which is used to design RF heating schemes.

name: Tunnel ionization (WKB/ADK) and ionization injection
summary: Quasi-static WKB tunnelling rates (Keldysh/ADK) decide where an intense pulse ionizes a gas. Wakefield accelerators use the steep field threshold of inner-shell tunnel ionization to inject electrons at a chosen phase of the wake (ionization injection).

name: Gamow tunnelling sets the fusion reactivity
summary: Fusion at 10–20 keV works only because nuclei tunnel through the Coulomb barrier. The barrier-penetration factor times the Maxwellian tail gives the Gamow peak. That peak fixes ⟨σv⟩, the best D–T temperature and the Lawson triple product.
sources: Lawson (1957). "Some Criteria for a Power Producing Thermonuclear Reactor". *Proc. Phys. Soc. B* 70, 6. [doi:10.1088/0370-1301/70/1/303](https://doi.org/10.1088/0370-1301/70/1/303)

name: Spin-polarized D–T fuel raises the fusion cross section
summary: D–T fusion goes mainly through the J=3/2⁺ resonance of ⁵He. Aligning the deuteron (spin 1) and triton (spin ½) spins puts every pair into J=3/2 and raises the cross section by a factor 3/2. Whether the polarization survives in a reactor plasma is still under study.

name: Landau damping of condensate collective modes
summary: At finite temperature, collective oscillations of a trapped Bose gas decay by Landau damping: energy passes resonantly to thermal Bogoliubov excitations at a rate set by the slope of their distribution. This is the same resonance logic as Landau damping of plasma waves.
map: E_k-E_i=\hbar\omega,\ \gamma\propto\partial f/\partial E\ \leftrightarrow\ v=\omega/k,\ \gamma\propto\partial f_0/\partial v
sources: Malmberg & Wharton (1964). "Collisionless Damping of Electrostatic Plasma Waves". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 13, 184. [doi:10.1103/PhysRevLett.13.184](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevLett.13.184)

name: Nonlinear Schrödinger: BEC solitons and Langmuir collapse
summary: The Gross–Pitaevskii equation and the envelope equation for Langmuir waves (Zakharov, with the ponderomotive density cavity) are both cubic nonlinear Schrödinger equations. Both show dark and bright solitons, modulational instability and collapse above a critical norm: the attractive-BEC 'bosenova' corresponds to Langmuir collapse and to laser self-focusing.
breaks: In a plasma, ψ is a classical wave envelope and the nonlinearity comes from the slow ion-acoustic density response, which is instantaneous only in the subsonic limit. In a BEC, ψ is the macroscopic wavefunction with contact interactions.

name: Quantized-vortex reconnection vs magnetic reconnection
summary: Superfluid vortex lines are frozen into the flow (Kelvin's theorem), as magnetic field lines are in a near-ideal plasma (Alfvén's theorem). Both can change topology only by reconnecting in a thin non-ideal region. Vortex reconnections in BECs and helium show X-point geometry and a universal separation law δ∝(t−t₀)^{1/2}.
map: \oint\mathbf v_s\cdot d\mathbf l=\kappa\,(h/m)\ \leftrightarrow\ \int\mathbf B\cdot d\mathbf S=\text{const (frozen-in)}
breaks: Superfluid circulation is quantized, and reconnection happens through the healing-length core of Gross–Pitaevskii dynamics. Magnetic flux is not quantized, and reconnection rates are set by resistivity, Hall/kinetic physics and plasmoids.

name: Partially degenerate electrons in warm dense matter
summary: Warm dense matter sits at θ=k_BT/E_F≈1, where electrons are neither classical nor fully degenerate. The finite-temperature Fermi-gas thermodynamics measured in ultracold Fermi gases sets its pressure. Strong coupling (Γ≈1) leaves no small parameter.

name: ICF adiabat: pressure over Fermi-degenerate pressure
summary: ICF designs keep the cold fuel close to a Fermi-degenerate state, because the work needed to compress it scales with degeneracy pressure. The 'adiabat' α=P/P_F measures the entropy that shocks add, and it limits the achievable areal density and gain.
sources: Nuckolls et al. (1972). "Laser Compression of Matter to Super-High Densities: Thermonuclear (CTR) Applications". *Nature* 239, 139. [doi:10.1038/239139a0](https://doi.org/10.1038/239139a0)

Lindl (1995). "Development of the indirect-drive approach to inertial confinement fusion and the target physics basis for ignition and gain". *Phys. Plasmas* 2, 3933. [doi:10.1063/1.871025](https://doi.org/10.1063/1.871025)

name: Debye screening → Thomas–Fermi screening for T≪T_F
summary: Linear-response screening of a test charge gives the Debye length in a classical plasma and the Thomas–Fermi length in a degenerate electron gas. The degeneracy parameter controls the crossover and separates classical from quantum plasmas (metals, white dwarfs, compressed fuel).

name: Path-integral Monte Carlo for warm dense matter
summary: Imaginary-time path integrals map quantum electrons and ions onto classical ring polymers. This gives first-principles equations of state and the warm-dense uniform electron gas used to build finite-temperature DFT functionals. The fermion sign problem limits the method at low θ and high density.
sources: Feynman (1948). "Space-Time Approach to Non-Relativistic Quantum Mechanics". *Rev. Mod. Phys.* 20, 367. [doi:10.1103/RevModPhys.20.367](https://doi.org/10.1103/RevModPhys.20.367)

name: X-ray Thomson scattering measures S(k,ω)
summary: X-ray Thomson scattering applies first-Born scattering theory to dense plasmas: the measured spectrum is the dynamic structure factor. The Chihara decomposition splits it into bound, free and screening-cloud parts. The scattering parameter decides between the collective (plasmon) and non-collective regimes, and the fit gives T_e, n_e and ionization.
sources: Glenzer & Redmer (2009). "X-ray Thomson scattering in high energy density plasmas". *Rev. Mod. Phys.* 81, 1625. [doi:10.1103/RevModPhys.81.1625](https://doi.org/10.1103/RevModPhys.81.1625)

name: Coulomb logarithm: Rutherford cross section, quantum cutoff
summary: Plasma collision operators (Landau, Lenard–Balescu, Fokker–Planck) integrate the Rutherford cross section over impact parameters. Debye screening cuts the integral off at large distance. At short distance the cutoff is the larger of the classical closest-approach distance and the de Broglie wavelength, and for hot electrons (T_e≳10Z² eV) that is the quantum one.

name: Ramsauer–Townsend minimum shapes argon discharges
summary: Ar, Kr and Xe are nearly transparent to electrons of ~0.2–0.7 eV because the s-wave phase shift passes through π. This minimum in the momentum-transfer cross section distorts electron energy distributions, mobility and breakdown in discharges. Partial-wave cross sections are fed into the Boltzmann solvers used for plasma processing.

name: Atomic spectroscopy as tokamak diagnostics (MSE, CXRS)
summary: Tokamaks read their internal state through atomic physics. The motional Stark effect on neutral-beam H-alpha light gives the current (q) profile. Charge-exchange recombination spectroscopy gives ion temperature and rotation. Impurity line radiation (e.g. tungsten) sets the core radiation losses.
map: \mathbf E_L=\mathbf v_b\times\mathbf B\Rightarrow\text{Stark-split }H_\alpha\text{ polarization}\to B_\theta/B_\phi\to q(r)

name: Atomic structure in dense plasma: IPD and opacity
summary: A dense plasma shifts and broadens atomic levels and lowers ionization thresholds (ionization-potential depression, pressure ionization). XFEL measurements disagreed with the standard Stewart–Pyatt model, and iron opacities measured on the Z machine exceed atomic-model predictions. Both remain unresolved tests of atomic structure in plasmas.

name: Ioffe–Pritchard atom traps borrow mirror-machine physics
summary: Magnetic traps hold weak-field-seeking atoms whose magnetic moment adiabatically follows B, just as a mirror holds gyrating particles through μ. The Ioffe–Pritchard trap took the Ioffe-bar minimum-B configuration from mirror fusion to remove the field zero, where Majorana spin flips (non-adiabatic loss) occur.
map: U=m_Fg_F\mu_B|\mathbf B|\ \leftrightarrow\ U_{eff}=\mu|\mathbf B|;\ \text{adiabatic if }\omega_L\gg|d\hat{\mathbf b}/dt|

name: Plasma echo ↔ spin echo: phase mixing vs decoherence
summary: Landau damping is phase mixing of free-streaming particles and can be undone, which produces plasma echoes, just as a Hahn echo reverses inhomogeneous dephasing (T_2^*) of spins. Collisions play the role of true decoherence (T_2), which no echo can recover.
breaks: Plasma phase mixing happens in a classical velocity continuum with no entanglement. Quantum decoherence needs system–environment entanglement and selects pointer states, which have no plasma counterpart.
sources: Malmberg & Wharton (1964). "Collisionless Damping of Electrostatic Plasma Waves". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 13, 184. [doi:10.1103/PhysRevLett.13.184](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevLett.13.184)
Zurek (2003). "Decoherence, einselection, and the quantum origins of the classical". *Rev. Mod. Phys.* 75, 715. [arXiv:quant-ph/0105127](https://arxiv.org/abs/quant-ph/0105127)

name: Wigner–Moyal equation reduces to Vlasov as ħ→0
summary: Wigner-transforming the von Neumann equation for a mean-field (Hartree) density matrix gives the Wigner–Poisson equation, which becomes the Vlasov equation as ħ→0. Quantum plasma kinetics, quantum Landau damping and the quantum Lenard–Balescu operator are all built on this map.

name: Wigner–Weyl wave kinetics of drift waves and zonal flows
summary: Phase-space quantum methods (Weyl symbols, Moyal brackets) have been brought in to treat drift-wave turbulence as a gas of 'driftons' interacting with zonal flows. This extends the ray (geometric-optics) wave-kinetic equation so that it captures zonal-flow stability and pattern formation.

name: Chirikov overlap: mirror traps to quantum kicked rotor
summary: Chirikov devised his resonance-overlap criterion (1959) for the breakdown of adiabatic confinement in magnetic mirror traps. It led to the standard map. The map's quantum version, the kicked rotor, shows dynamical localization (realized with cold atoms) and became a founding model of quantum chaos.

name: Quantum algorithms for Vlasov and plasma-wave simulation
summary: Linear plasma problems (linearized Vlasov, cold-plasma waves) can be cast as Hamiltonian simulation on qubits, and nonlinear Vlasov dynamics through Koopman–von Neumann or Carleman embeddings. It is still open whether an end-to-end speed-up survives state preparation, readout and nonlinearity.

name: Brillouin light–sound coupling: optomechanics vs SBS
summary: In stimulated Brillouin scattering, a laser decays into scattered light plus an ion-acoustic wave driven by the ponderomotive force. This is the plasma counterpart of the radiation-pressure or electrostrictive coupling of light to a mechanical mode in Brillouin optomechanics. Both obey the same phase-matched three-wave coupled-mode equations.
map: H_{int}=\hbar g_0a^\dagger a(b+b^\dagger)\ \leftrightarrow\ \omega_0=\omega_s+\omega_{ia},\ \mathbf k_0=\mathbf k_s+\mathbf k_{ia}
breaks: Plasma SBS is classical, convective and broadband, with strongly Landau-damped acoustic modes, and it is a loss to suppress. Optomechanics uses discrete high-Q modes run near the quantum ground state.
sources: Aspelmeyer, Kippenberg & Marquardt (2014). "Cavity optomechanics". *Rev. Mod. Phys.* 86, 1391. [arXiv:1303.0733](https://arxiv.org/abs/1303.0733)

name: Plasma parametric decay ↔ parametric down-conversion
summary: Stimulated Raman scattering and two-plasmon decay split a pump photon into two daughter waves that match energy and momentum. This is the classical, stimulated limit of the three-wave Hamiltonian that produces squeezed vacuum by parametric down-conversion. Plasma Raman amplifiers use the same gain.
breaks: The plasma daughters (Langmuir waves) are heavily damped and grow from thermal noise, so quantum correlations and squeezing are destroyed. Down-conversion uses a nearly lossless χ^(2) crystal starting from vacuum.

name: Photon in plasma: effective mass ħω_p; plasmons
summary: Transverse waves in a plasma obey ω²=ω_p²+c²k², a massive Klein–Gordon dispersion. So photons in a plasma act as quasiparticles of mass ħω_p/c², which lets them decay into neutrino pairs in stars. Quantized longitudinal Langmuir oscillations are plasmons.
breaks: The mass is a medium effect tied to the plasma rest frame, and longitudinal and transverse modes differ. No vacuum gauge symmetry is broken; this is the analogy behind the Anderson–Higgs mechanism, not an identity with it.
sources: Bohm & Gross (1949). "Theory of Plasma Oscillations. A. Origin of Medium-Like Behavior". *Phys. Rev.* 75, 1851. [doi:10.1103/PhysRev.75.1851](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRev.75.1851)

name: Transmon frequency = Josephson plasma frequency
summary: A transmon's transition frequency is set by the Josephson plasma frequency, named by analogy with Langmuir oscillation. The Josephson (kinetic) inductance resonates with the junction capacitance, as electron inertia (kinetic inductance m/ne²) resonates with the space-charge restoring force to give ω_p.
breaks: A single junction is a one-degree-of-freedom anharmonic LC oscillator, with no Debye screening and no many-particle collective dynamics. Only in bulk layered superconductors is the Josephson plasma resonance a true collective mode.
sources: Koch et al. (2007). "Charge-insensitive qubit design derived from the Cooper pair box". *Phys. Rev. A* 76, 042319. [arXiv:cond-mat/0703002](https://arxiv.org/abs/cond-mat/0703002)

name: Bohm potential in quantum hydrodynamics of dense plasma
summary: The Madelung (de Broglie–Bohm) rewriting of the Schrödinger equation supplies the 'Bohm potential' term used in quantum hydrodynamic models of dense and warm dense plasmas. Its validity and prefactor beyond the long-wavelength limit are disputed.
sources: Bohm (1952). "A Suggested Interpretation of the Quantum Theory in Terms of 'Hidden' Variables. I". *Phys. Rev.* 85, 166. [doi:10.1103/PhysRev.85.166](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRev.85.166)

name: Antihydrogen: trap plasmas meet precision spectroscopy
summary: Antihydrogen is made by merging antiproton and positron plasmas in Penning–Malmberg traps, using rotating-wall compression and evaporative and sympathetic cooling. It is then probed by 1S–2S and hyperfine spectroscopy and compared with hydrogen to test CPT symmetry.
